div.head: Excom X 1
div.ab: Ex auctoritate Dei patris omnipotentis et Filii eius, domini nostri Iesu Christi, et in uirtute Spiritus sancti et beate gloriose Dei genitricis semper uirginis Marie, sanctissimi archangeli Michaelis et omnium sanctorum angelorum et archangelorum, sancti Iohannis baptiste et omnium sanctorum patriarcharum et prophetarum, apostolorum principis sancti Petri et omnium apostolorum et euangelistarum, sancti Adhelberti et omnium sanctorum martyrum, sanctissimi confessoris Benedicti et omnium sanctorum confessorum, sancte Marie Magdalene et omnium sanctarum uirginum et celestium uirtutum, omniumque simul sauctorum tociusque ordinis nostri ministerii,
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 440 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s heading: [X. aus Vd]; Liebermann’s print has ‘sauctorum’ (a turned n; read ‘sanctorum’); transcribed as printed; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c. 1000–c. 1200 (Liebermann)”, now “c. 1000–c. 1200 (Liebermann, I p. 440)”)

note.seg: X steht Excom. VIII am nächsten und stammt, wegen Adhelberti in 1, vielleicht aus Hereford.
X is closest to Excom. VIII and, on account of Adhelberti in 1, perhaps comes from Hereford.
